problem: The closing claim 'x is easier because its elimination needs no differentiation' is false. Eliminating y is done by applying D to the first equation (D²x + 2Dy = 3), which does differentiate the known right side 3t into 3. Eliminating x, as the answer itself shows, also needs one application of D (to the second equation). Both routes need exactly one differentiation, so the stated reason is wrong and would mislead a student about when D acts on a known function of t.
fix: 'Either unknown works; each elimination needs exactly one application of D. Eliminating y differentiates the right side 3t into 3, while eliminating x differentiates the equation 3x + Dy = 0 and then uses Dx = 3t − 2y.'

problem: Saying a zero operator determinant means 'the equations are dependent' covers only one case. When the determinant is zero the equations may also be inconsistent, for example Dx + y = t and Dx + y = 1 have determinant zero yet no solution at all.
fix: 'If the operator determinant works out to zero, the two equations are dependent (they then have infinitely many solutions) or inconsistent (no solution); check which before dividing.'
